Mikolow Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Mikołów, Poland

Demolished. This is the older of Mikołów's two Jewish cemeteries, presumably established in the 17th century, as indicated by a record from the historian Marcus Brann documenting the burial of a man named Moses on January 28. It remained in active use until the early 18th century, when the Jewish community established the newer cemetery documented elsewhere in this collection. At the beginning of the 20th century, the site held a small lapidarium of two matzevot built into a brick wall, one commemorating a woman named Chaja who died March 7, 1722. At the end of the 1960s, the site became part of a residential development, and by 1989 the plot had been taken over for an elementary school, built 1985–1988, destroying all remaining aboveground traces.
